system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter

**Overall read:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." It collapses fundamental/title claims into the general regime, uses blanket data-room disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge bar to neutralise the warranties, and leaves every identified DD risk (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy incident) either unquantified or pushed post-Completion. The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us: it candidly confirms that none of the key consents, releases, payments or verifications are in the data room. Recommendation: reject and re-mark across the board; several items should be conditions precedent or price adjustments, not warranty matters.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2m–12m), with fundamental/title/tax and specific indemnities outside the cap (or capped at 100%).
- Recommendation: Counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m) and carve out fundamental, tax, IP and the specific indemnities. Reason: 20% is the bottom of the Australian mid-market range and only works if the known risks are dealt with separately — they aren't.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: De minimis ~AUD 10,000–12,000 (≈0.05%), basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%), tipping (first-dollar) basket, and related claims aggregated.
- Recommendation: Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 150k tipping basket; aggregate linked claims (e.g. the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals). Reason: an excess-only basket plus a high de minimis structurally wipes out the mid-size claims that are most likely in a AUD 24m SaaS deal.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months; limitation language applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; 6–7 years for fundamental/title; indemnity claims limited only by statute.
- Recommendation: Counter 24 months general, 7 years tax/fundamental; strike the default "applies to all Claims" wording. Reason: 18 months captures only one full post-Completion financial year and the default-to-all-Claims drafting is a back-door cap on indemnities.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, 6-year (or statutory) limitation, no de minimis/basket.
- Recommendation: Reject outright; non-negotiable. Reason: if title to the shares fails, recovering 20% of the price over 18 months is not a remedy — "administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). No fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment carve-out appears.
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful default and wilful concealment by the Seller or the Company/its officers.
- Recommendation: Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out; also preserve statutory rights (e.g. ACL misleading-conduct claims cannot be contracted out of). Reason: a cap that purports to cover fraud is unenforceable in any event and signals the drafting is one-sided — fix it rather than litigate it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: Disclosure limited to matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; no general data-room or public-register disclosure; disclosure against specific warranties only.
- Recommendation: Reject general disclosure; accept specific disclosures 2–10 only, with a "fairly disclosed" standard. Reason: blanket data-room disclosure converts every warranty into "the data room is accurate," shifting all DD risk to us.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller (cl 8.3): No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- Buyer wants: Delete, or at most limit to actual knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, and only of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter (no constructive/imputed/adviser knowledge, no "discoverable").
- Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3 entirely; fallback to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals. Reason: "discoverable" plus adviser knowledge makes the warranties illusory and invites a satellite dispute about what our lawyers "should have found."

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: Reasonable endeavours; CP treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: Hard CP — unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen), in agreed form, no adverse variation to the Bluefen contract; Seller "best endeavours"; Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the Long Stop Date; price adjustment or escrow if Bluefen revenue is lost within 12 months.
- Recommendation: Hold firm on an unconditional-consent CP in agreed form; do not accept the "deemed satisfied" mechanic. Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) — a consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is not a consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge of security.
- Buyer wants: Repayment of the full payout figure from the Seller's proceeds at Completion via funds flow, with executed deed of release and PPSR/security discharges delivered at Completion (or at minimum a bank payout letter and undertaking to release). Change-of-control under cl 8.1 must be waived or the facility repaid before Completion.
- Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release; make repayment, release and discharge Completion deliverables funded from the price. Reason: this is a debt-free/cash-free deal — a AUD 3.2m facility in default on change-of-control with security still on foot would mean we paid AUD 24m for an encumbered company.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k) are "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure Letter 5 confirms they are not in the funds flow and on-costs are unknown.
- Buyer wants: Bonuses plus payroll tax, superannuation and all on-costs (grossed up — likely ~AUD 490k–520k) treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, expressly itemised in the funds flow; specific indemnity for any shortfall or retention-condition dispute.
- Recommendation: Itemise in funds flow as a price deduction with on-costs and a specific indemnity. Reason: "a matter for the Seller" means nothing if the Company is the employer and the liability crystallises on Completion inside the entity we are buying.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate." Disclosure Letter 4 confirms no receipt, no confirmatory assignment, and cl 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- Buyer wants: CP or Completion deliverable — proof of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral-rights consents from Ironquay; uncapped (or price-capped) specific indemnity for loss arising from any defect in title to the SOW3 Project Materials, not merely the AUD 180k.
- Recommendation: Require payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; expand the indemnity to cover loss of IP, not the invoice. Reason: the exposure is loss of ownership of developed product IP, which could be worth multiples of the AUD 180k unpaid fee.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter 6 confirms ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address, access/scope unknown, notification obligation unassessed.
- Buyer wants: Completion of the investigation and an OAIC Notifiable Data Breach assessment (30-day statutory window under the Privacy Act is likely already running from discovery) before Completion; specific indemnity (outside cap/basket/time limits) for all costs, regulator action, notification, remediation, third-party claims and contract breaches (including any Bluefen/Mossvale data clauses) arising from DD-006; conduct-of-claims rights; warranty of no other incidents.
- Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus a pre-Completion completed assessment; reject "not material." Reason: a disclosed, unassessed incident is the textbook case for a specific indemnity — once disclosed, it is otherwise carved out of the warranties and we would bear it entirely.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter 8 says to read DD-008 and DD-011 together and does not say they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Buyer wants: Clarity on whether these are one contract split into three (relevant to de minimis gaming), whether already committed/accrued pre-Completion, and whether they are in the FY27 budget on which the price was struck; if committed pre-Completion and unbudgeted, treat as Debt-like item or price adjustment; aggregation clause so the three count as one claim.
- Recommendation: Seek confirmation; adjust price for any pre-Completion unbudgeted commitment and insert claim-aggregation language. Reason: three AUD 110k items sitting just above a AUD 25k de minimis and summing to just above the basket look structured, and "ordinary course" is asserted, not evidenced.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: One regime for everything — general, fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims all subject to the same cap, thresholds, 18-month limit and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance clauses.
- Buyer wants: Four distinct tiers: (i) general warranties — cap/basket/24 months; (ii) fundamental/title — 100% cap, 6+ years, no thresholds; (iii) tax and IP — 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds (or tax covenant); (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006) — uncapped or price-capped, no thresholds, statutory limitation.
- Recommendation: Restructure Schedule/cl 12 into separate tiers with an express "limitations in cl 12 do not apply to" list. Reason: a single-tier regime lets known, quantified risks be absorbed by a cap designed for unknown ones.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter 10 notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: Independent verification — current ASIC extract, review of the constitution for pre-emptive/consent requirements, option/convertible/ESOP register, PPSR search against the Seller and Company (Riverlark security may extend to shares), chain-of-title for share transfers, and a fundamental title warranty (clean, unencumbered, fully paid, no options) with 100% cap.
- Recommendation: Run the searches now; do not rely on the Company's own register; retain full fundamental title warranty. Reason: a share register maintained by the Seller's company is self-certification, and the Riverlark security may be over the shares themselves.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket).
- Buyer wants: Separate tax warranties plus a full tax indemnity/covenant for pre-Completion tax (7-year limitation, 100% cap, no basket), covering income tax, GST, payroll tax (relevant to the bonuses), FBT and super guarantee; IP warranties on ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments (relevant to Ironquay), open-source compliance — 100% cap, 6–7 years.
- Recommendation: Reject "settled"; insert standalone tax indemnity and elevate IP to the fundamental tier. Reason: for a data-analytics business, IP is the asset being bought and tax exposure runs for years past an 18-month window — neither fits the general regime.

---

**Priority sequencing for the mark-up:** (1) Riverlark repayment/release at Completion; (2) Bluefen unconditional consent CP; (3) category separation and fundamental/tax/IP tier; (4) delete cl 8.3 and general disclosure; (5) specific indemnities for DD-005, DD-006, Ironquay; then (6) cap/basket/time-limit numbers. Items 1–5 go to deal certainty and whether we are actually acquiring a debt-free company with its key contract and IP intact; the numbers in item 6 are secondary once the known risks are ring-fenced.

Happy to turn this into a redline of cl 12 and the CP schedule, or an issues list for the next call with Harbourglass's counsel.
=== END ADVICE ===
